emergence.summary: A single-gene TTR proteinopathy: destabilising TTR variants (e.g. Val30Met, Val122Ile) let the transthyretin tetramer dissociate, misfold and deposit as amyloid fibrils in peripheral nerve and heart, progressively SUPPRESSING nerve and cardiac function. Like Huntington, the toxic GAIN is read as an over-active pathological BRAKE on organ function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), and the kit re-derives the approved therapies, which REMOVE the toxic species rather than treating symptoms: TTR-lowering silencers (patisiran / vutrisiran siRNA; inotersen / eplontersen antisense) and a tetramer STABILISER (tafamidis) that blocks dissociation/misfolding; in-vivo CRISPR knockdown is clinical. The gamma read is of the TTR locus switch structure; the destabilising point mutations are coding changes outside the promoter firewall. (The non-hereditary wild-type form, ATTRwt, is an age/conformational aggregation of normal TTR, not a germline sequence lesion, and is outside this single-gene read.) Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: nerve and cardiac tissue function (progressively suppressed by TTR amyloid deposition)

grades.perturbation_direction: [F] forced by (role x mechanism); cited biology
grades.perturbation_magnitude: [O] OPEN -- how far the switch moves is runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable

per_gene.note: TTR encodes transthyretin, normally a stable tetrameric transport protein (thyroxine / retinol-binding protein). Destabilising variants promote tetramer dissociation and misfolding into amyloid; the deposited fibrils act as a toxic GAIN that SUPPRESSES nerve and cardiac function -- read here as an over-active pathological BRAKE on organ function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), the same proteinopathy framing used for Huntington. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the destabilising coding lesion's magnitude (firewall).

emergence.firewall: gamma reads promoter switch-threshold STRUCTURE only; perturbation DIRECTION is forced+cited; MAGNITUDE is [O] (runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable).

levers.push_direction: lower circulating TTR so less amyloidogenic protein is available to deposit -> relieve the suppression of organ function
levers.agent_class: TTR-lowering siRNA / antisense (patisiran / vutrisiran; inotersen / eplontersen)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] TTR-lowering magnitude / progression-slowing not derived from sequence
levers.src: Adams 2018 NEJM (patisiran); Benson 2018 NEJM (inotersen); APOLLO-B / vutrisiran

falsifiers.claim: TTR amyloid acts as an over-active brake suppressing nerve / cardiac function (axis DOWN)
falsifiers.falsifier: if reducing or stabilising TTR (removing the aggregate) WORSENED organ function, the suppressing-brake direction would be refuted
falsifiers.measurable_by: neuropathy / cardiac function vs amyloid burden under TTR lowering or stabilisation

falsifiers.claim: lowering or stabilising TTR (reduce / correct) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if lowering circulating TTR or stabilising the tetramer failed to slow, or accelerated, amyloid progression, the lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: amyloid deposition / clinical progression vs TTR-lowering or stabilisation
